explanation: No Mathlib declaration mentions `ofFunctorColimIso`/`ofFunctorColimitι` (grep over Mathlib for `ofFunctorColim*` gives nothing; Mathlib's `Algebra/Homology/HomologicalComplexLimits.lean` only has `coconeOfHasColimitEval` for `F : J ⥤ HomologicalComplex C c`, a different direction). The theorem is however exactly the Mathlib lemma `IsColimit.comp_coconePointUniqueUpToIso_hom` (dual of `IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv_comp`, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/IsLimit.lean:163, inside `namespace IsColimit`) at the specific instance: `ofFunctorColimitι D t` has `n`-th component `colimit.ι (D ⋙ eval A shape n) t` and `(ofFunctorColimIso D).hom` is `Hom.isoOfComponents` whose `n`-th component is precisely `(colimit.isColimit (D ⋙ eval A shape n)).coconePointUniqueUpToIso (isColimitOfPreserves (eval A shape n) (colimit.isColimit D))`, so after `ext n` the goal is the instance `s.ι.app t ≫ (coconePointUniqueUpToIso P Q).hom = t.ι.app t`, solved by the single Mathlib lemma (as the library's own one-line proof shows). Since the statement is a two-line corollary of that general colimit lemma, it is a special case rather than a literal restatement.
